newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slip in narrow early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slip in narrow early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened weaker but quickly came off lows in narrow range trade on Tuesday, after Wall Street's mixed performance overnight and ahead of a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on interest rates, brokers said.
"The market is waiting to see what happens in New York," said Ronald Lam, chief dealer at Dao Heng Securities. "It is difficult to assess the (Hong Kong) market trend right now."
The blue-chip Hang Seng Index was 13 points down at 11,609.00 after 30 minutes of trade on Tuesday, after dropping to a low of 11,568.

Brokers said the market was likely to take a breather until it sees what the Fed's policy-setting body, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), decides regarding interest rates when it meets later on Tuesday, as well as the New York market reaction.

Turnover leapt to HK$5.89 billion, including two major share placements, 55 million shares worth HK$3.5 billion by Henderson Land and 250 million shares worth HK$1.55 billion by COSCO Pacific. Turnover at the same time on Monday morning was a moderate HK$900 million.
The Henderson Land and COSCO Pacific placements also took the market by surprise, brokers said.
"The Henderson placement was unexpected because the company just announced a big dividend payout," said Lam.
Henderson Land shares tumbled HK$2.00 to HK$64.25.

The company announced a final dividend of HK$1.43 per share and a special bonus dividend of HK$1.00 per share when it announced its final results in mid-September, and the share had climbed to record highs since then.
COSCO Pacific's placement of 250 million shares amounted to 13.4 percent of the company's enlarged share capital. Its shares dropped HK$0.25 to HK$6.30.
Despite the cash calls, analysts and brokers were still bullish on the outlook for the market, saying the market's bull trend was still in tact and any pullback would be short.
They added that a 25 basis point rise in U.S. and Hong Kong lending rates had already been factored into market prices.
Properties led the market down on Tuesday morning, chiefly due to the sharp drop in Henderson Land.
Finance counters were also weak. Both HSBC and Hang Seng Bank shed HK$0.50 to trade at HK$141.50 and HK$79.00.
